title: Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah undertakes a review of the security of Siliguri corridor
subtitle:
Home Minister reviews the status of all infrastructural projects being undertaken in Siliguri Corridor that are critical to its security
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India is committed to making the security of the Siliguri Corridor impregnable
Issues related to PIO activities, demographic changes, illegal immigration and the border affairs were also discussed
Shri Amit Shah stressed upon the concept of quadrangular approach to border security and directed all agencies to implement it in full spirit
Union Home Minister directs all agencies present to increase their footprints in the corridor by establishing more of their institutions
Directions also issued to keep Siliguri Corridor free of encroachments
Shri Amit Shah underscores the need to take all steps to stop illegal immigration in the Siliguri Corridor
body_text:
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah undertook a review of the security of Siliguri corridor, which was attended by senior officials of central and state Ministries, including MHA, MoRTH, Army, BSF, SSB and RPF, apart from Chief Secretary and DGP West Bengal. During the meeting, which was also attended by CM, West Bengal, the Multi Agency Centre’s (MAC)Standing Focus Group on Siliguri Corridor (SFG-SC) made presentation about progress made so far and its recommendations towards further strengthening the security of the Siliguri corridor.
During the meeting, Union Home Minister further reviewed the status of all infrastructural projects being undertaken in Siliguri Corridor that are critical to its security. He also discussed issues related to PIO activities, demographic changes, illegal immigration and the border affairs. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India is committed to making the security of the Siliguri Corridor impregnable.
In the meeting, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stressed upon the concept of quadrangular approach to border security and directed all agencies to implement it in full spirit. Emphasising the criticality of infrastructural projects in the corridor, Shri Shah directed all agencies present to complete all pending works in time bound manner.
Union Home Minister directed all agencies present to increase their footprints in the corridor by establishing more of their institutions. He also reviewed security of all Vital Installations on the corridor and directed that all necessary steps be taken to secure them. He further directed to keep Siliguri Corridor free of encroachments. He underscored the need to take all steps to stop illegal immigration in the Siliguri Corridor.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah suggested to Chief Minister, West Bengal to explore possibilities of opening more Sainik schools in North Bengal. He further asked the Chief Minister to work towards increasing the number of senior NCC cadets in North Bengal. He also urged State Government to strengthen the institution of Civil Defense and Home Guards in Siliguri Corridor.

enrichment.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah reviewed the security of the strategically vital Siliguri Corridor in a meeting attended by central and West Bengal state officials, the Army, BSF, SSB, RPF and West Bengal's Chief Minister. He reviewed infrastructure projects critical to the corridor's security, discussed illegal immigration, demographic change and PIO activities, and directed agencies to adopt a 'quadrangular approach' to border security, remove encroachments, and expand institutional presence in the area.
enrichment.context:
The Siliguri Corridor, popularly called the 'Chicken's Neck', is a narrow strip of land (about 22 km wide at its narrowest) in West Bengal connecting mainland India to its Northeastern states. It is flanked by Nepal and Bangladesh on one side and Bhutan on the other, with China's Chumbi Valley in close proximity, making it one of India's most strategically sensitive geographic chokepoints. Any disruption here—whether through infrastructure vulnerability, illegal immigration, demographic shifts, or hostile activity—could sever connectivity to the Northeast, giving the corridor outsized importance in India's internal and external security calculus.

The review comes amid recurring concerns about illegal immigration from Bangladesh, cross-border demographic change, and the activities of persons of Indian origin (PIO) in border areas, issues that have featured in India's border management discourse for years, including debates around the National Register of Citizens and border fencing along the India-Bangladesh frontier. The Multi Agency Centre's Standing Focus Group on Siliguri Corridor reflects institutionalised, multi-agency coordination (MHA, MoRTH, armed forces, paramilitary, railways, and state government) to safeguard the corridor, and the Home Minister's push for a 'quadrangular approach' signals an attempt to synchronise security, infrastructure, demographic monitoring, and administrative presence in a unified strategy.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Siliguri Corridor', often referred to as the 'Chicken's Neck', is strategically important because it:
options: Connects the Indian mainland to the Northeastern states
Serves as India's largest inland waterway terminus
Forms the boundary between Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
Is the primary trade corridor with Sri Lanka
prelims_questions.explanation: The Siliguri Corridor is a narrow strip of land in West Bengal that links mainland India to its Northeastern states, flanked by Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and close to China's Chumbi Valley, making it a critical strategic chokepoint.

prelims_questions.question: In the context of the Multi Agency Centre (MAC) mentioned in the review of Siliguri Corridor security, MAC functions primarily as a body for:
options: Coordinating intelligence sharing among security and intelligence agencies
Regulating foreign direct investment in border states
Issuing passports to residents of border districts
Managing customs duties on cross-border trade
prelims_questions.explanation: The Multi Agency Centre (MAC), under the Intelligence Bureau, is India's principal platform for sharing intelligence inputs among central and state security agencies, including on issues like border security.

mains_questions.question: The Siliguri Corridor is often called India's most vulnerable strategic chokepoint. Discuss the geographical and geopolitical factors that make its security critical, and suggest measures to secure it.
Illegal immigration and demographic change in border areas pose significant internal security challenges. Examine the issue with reference to India's northeastern and eastern border regions.

study_notes.reason: The Siliguri Corridor's geography and strategic significance are a well-defined factual core UPSC could test directly, while the meeting's discussion of illegal immigration, demographic change and the 'quadrangular approach' offers real analytical material on border management and federal coordination.

prelims.point: Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck') is a narrow strip (~22 km at narrowest) in West Bengal connecting mainland India to the Northeast
prelims.why_important: A classic factual/locational item UPSC frequently uses for map-based or statement-based questions on India's strategic chokepoints.

prelims.point: The corridor is flanked by Nepal and Bangladesh on one side, Bhutan on the other, with China's Chumbi Valley nearby
prelims.why_important: Tests precise knowledge of the corridor's neighbouring countries, a detail easily confused or tested via elimination-based statements.

prelims.point: Multi Agency Centre's (MAC) Standing Focus Group on Siliguri Corridor (SFG-SC) coordinates security review
prelims.why_important: An institutional detail on multi-agency border coordination mechanisms that could appear in questions on internal security architecture.

prelims.point: Agencies involved in corridor security include BSF, SSB and RPF alongside the Army
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing mandates of BSF (international border), SSB (Nepal/Bhutan border) and RPF (railway security) is a recurring UPSC distinction-testing pattern.

mains.point: The corridor's narrowness and proximity to three international borders and China's Chumbi Valley make it India's most critical strategic chokepoint for Northeast connectivity
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'Discuss the strategic significance of the Siliguri Corridor for India's security' type questions.

mains.point: Illegal immigration and demographic change in border areas raise concerns of altered ethnic composition and internal security vulnerabilities
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on challenges of illegal immigration and demographic change along India's eastern border, linking to NRC-type debates.

mains.point: The 'quadrangular approach' signals an attempt to integrate security, infrastructure, demographic monitoring and institutional presence into one strategy
mains.analytical_use: Can be cited as an example of evolving multi-dimensional border security doctrine in 'suggest measures to secure vulnerable corridors' answers.

mains.point: Central-state coordination (MHA, Army, BSF, SSB, RPF with West Bengal government) reflects cooperative federalism in security matters
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on the role of state governments in matters constitutionally under central security agencies' purview.

mains.point: PIO (Persons of Indian Origin) activities and encroachments in the corridor are flagged as security concerns requiring administrative and infrastructural remedies
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to discuss non-traditional threats and administrative gaps in securing strategic land corridors.

low_priority.point: Suggestion to open more Sainik Schools and increase NCC cadets in North Bengal
low_priority.reason: A policy suggestion without concrete commitment or data, more administrative/ceremonial than examinable.

low_priority.point: Call to strengthen Civil Defence and Home Guards institutions
low_priority.reason: Generic administrative directive lacking specific testable or analytical substance.
